historical_references.reference: Jaitra-kaala or Jaitra-yuga is the name of a mythological period mentioned in Hindu scriptures during which the gods and demons churned the primordial ocean (Samudra-manthan) to obtain the elixir of immortality (Amrita). Lord Indra, the king of gods, in the guise of Mohini, a female avatar, was able to distract the demon king Mahasur during this process, enabling the gods to complete their task. The term 'Jetendra' is derived from 'Jaitra-kaala'.

historical_references.reference: Jayantasena, popularly known as Sena I or Mahasena, was a legendary king of the ancient Shakya (Shakya-vansa) kingdom in Magadha, modern-day Bihar, India. He is believed to have ruled during the late Gupta period (c. 561-606 CE). The name 'Jetendra' was used as a title by later kings in the Shakya dynasty, including Anandakumar Jain, who was the last Maharaja of Darbhanga in 1912 before the princely state was merged into the British Indian empire.
